A case constructed for teaching: the underlying MRI is real (public archive, patient with endometrioid carcinoma of the endometrium); the endometrioma was added by computer in all sequences with the noise of the original image. The realism is good but simplified (regular shape, no effect on adjacent organs).
Endometrioma on MRI: hyperintense on T1, remains hyperintense on T1 FS (blood, not fat); on T2 it is hypointense with “shading” (concentrated hemoglobin degradation products, often with a dependent gradient); the “T2 dark spot” is highly specific. Often multiple or bilateral, with adhesions (“kissing ovaries”).
Differential diagnosis: functional hemorrhagic cyst (T1 hyperintense but without marked shading, shrinks at follow-up after 6-12 weeks), mature teratoma (loses signal with fat suppression), lesions with enhancing solid components (suspicious: malignant transformation, more frequent after age 45 and above 6-9 cm).
After contrast the blood content remains hyperintense: to look for enhancing solid tissue, subtraction images are needed.
O-RADS MRI: endometrioma without solid tissue = 2 (almost certainly benign).
Lesione annessiale iperintensa in T1: gu: Adnexal lesion hyperintense on T1: look at the T1 FS. It stays bright = blood (endometrioma); it turns dark = fat (dermoid).
